problems.title: Implement Trie (Prefix Tree)
problems.statement: Implement a trie data structure supporting insert(word), search(word), and startsWith(prefix).
problems.understanding: A Trie stores strings character-by-character as a tree. Each node tracks its children and whether a complete word ends there.

naive.title: Naive Solution — Brute Force
naive.html: Store all words in a list and perform string operations on every query.

problems.intuition: Store characters in a tree where each edge is a character. Traverse character-by-character for O(L) insert, search, and prefix checks.
problems.approach:
1. Define TrieNode with children = {} and is_word = False.
  2. insert(word): Walk node-by-node from root, creating missing children. Set node.is_word = True at last character.
  3. search(word): Walk node-by-node. Return False if any character is missing. Return node.is_word at end.
  4. startsWith(prefix): Same traversal as search but return True regardless of is_word at end.
problems.takeaway: Pattern — Efficient prefix lookup → Trie (Hash Map per node)

problems.title: Design Add and Search Words Data Structure
problems.statement: Design a data structure supporting addWord(word) and search(word) where '.' in search patterns matches any single character.
problems.understanding: A wildcard '.' means branching into every child of the current Trie node simultaneously — a DFS over all children.

naive.title: Naive Solution — Brute Force
naive.html: Store words in a list and compare each candidate against the search pattern character-by-character.

problems.intuition: Build a Trie for fast prefix traversal. When encountering '.', branch into all children via DFS and return True if any branch succeeds.
problems.approach:
1. Build Trie with TrieNode(children, is_word) exactly as LC 208.
  2. addWord inserts into the Trie identically.
  3. search(word) calls dfs(index, node).
  4. Base case: index == len(word) → return node.is_word.
  5. If word[index] != '.': advance into node.children[char] if exists.
  6. If word[index] == '.': iterate all node.children.values() and return True if any recursive call returns True.

optimal.title: Optimized Code (Python 3)
complexity: addWord: O(L), search: O(L) normal / O(26^L) worst with wildcards
Space: O(total chars) + O(L) DFS stack

problems.takeaway: Pattern — Trie + DFS Backtracking for wildcard branching

problems.title: Word Search II
problems.statement: Given an m x n board of characters and a list of strings words, return all words from the list that can be found in the board (adjacent horizontal/vertical cells, no cell reused).
problems.understanding: Running separate board-DFS for each word is wasteful when words share prefixes. A Trie over all words enables prefix pruning — a non-matching prefix stops all further exploration.

naive.title: Naive Solution — Brute Force
naive.html: For every word, start a full board DFS from every matching cell.

problems.intuition: Build a single Trie from all words. Run one DFS from every board cell navigating the Trie simultaneously. When the current character is not in the Trie node's children, prune immediately — this avoids exploring invalid prefixes shared across many words.
problems.approach:
1. Build Trie from all words, storing node.word = word (not is_word) at terminal nodes.
  2. Outer loops: iterate every board cell (r, c) and call dfs(r, c, root).
  3. DFS checks: out-of-bounds, visited marker '#', or char not in node.children → return immediately.
  4. If next_node.word is not None: append to result and set next_node.word = None to prevent duplicates.
  5. Mark cell board[r][c] = '#', recurse in 4 directions with next_node, then restore cell.

optimal.title: Optimized Code (Python 3)
complexity: Time: O(R × C × 4^L) with prefix pruning
Space: O(total chars in words) + O(L) stack

problems.takeaway: Pattern — Multi-word board search → Trie + DFS + Backtracking + Prefix Pruning
